memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The woman said to the serpent, "We may eat fruit from the trees in the garden, but God did say, 'You must not eat fruit from the tree that is in the middle of the garden, and you must not touch it, or you will die.'" — Gen 3:2–3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At first glance, Eve seems to be defending God. The serpent had twisted His words, and she steps in to correct him. But look a little closer, and something has already gone wrong.

God had said they must not eat from that one tree (Gen 2:17). Eve adds something God never said — "and you must not touch it." She also softens the warning. God had said "you will surely die," but in her mouth it becomes only "you will die." In just one sentence, she has both added to God's command and toned down its seriousness.

This is a gentle warning for us. We can drift not only by ignoring God's Word, but by quietly editing it — adding rules He never gave, or softening truths that feel uncomfortable. Both leave us standing on shaky ground when temptation presses in.

Dear friend, God's Word does not need our additions, and it does not need our softening. It is perfect as He gave it (Ps 19:7). The safest place to stand is on Scripture exactly as it is written — the same solid ground where Jesus stood and never once wavered (Matt 4:4).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there commands of God you have quietly added to, making faith heavier than He intended?
2. Are there warnings in Scripture you have softened because they feel uncomfortable?
3. How can you grow to know God's Word more accurately this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your Word is perfect and trustworthy just as You gave it. Guard my heart from adding to it or softening it, and help me to hold Your truth exactly as it stands. Amen.
